s: Redis, CDN, HTTP caching, cache invalidation, patterns
d: Caching is the single most impactful performance optimization. Redis stores data in-memory for microsecond reads. CDNs cache assets globally. HTTP headers prevent unnecessary requests. But cache invalidation is genuinely one of the hardest problems in CS.
c: Redis data types: String Hash List Set ZSet Stream

p: Caching stores copies of frequently accessed data in extremely fast, in-memory datastores (like Redis or Memcached) to reduce database load and speed up API response times.
2. Check cache (Cache Hit?). If yes, return data immediately.
3. If no (Cache Miss), query primary DB.
4. Save DB result to cache with a TTL (Time To Live), then return.

// Cache Aside Pattern
const cachedUser = await redis.get(`user:${id}`);
if (cachedUser) return JSON.parse(cachedUser);

const user = await db.users.findById(id);
await redis.setex(`user:${id}`, 3600, JSON.stringify(user)); // 1 hour TTL
return user;
